profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Medchat·ai & Elegant Machine
profile.summary:
Hi there!

My name is Layton. I'm a web application engineer with a strong focus on UI, UX and application architecture. I'm all about making fully responsive, easy to use, intuitive web applications.

I work hard to write scalable code that will cost you less to maintain and be easy for developers to understand and work with. I am very strong at prototyping (rapid iteration is a specialty of mine), improving on user experience and interactions, and thinking ahead to solve functional, usability, and architectural problems before they arise.

I have extensive experience working with national and international teams, including having worked as a lead/architect.

Some of my experience (chronologically):

 - I am currently a web application engineer at MedChat, where we are growing the single best HIPAA compliant chat application in the healthcare industry. It's a team workflow tool as well as a patient communication platform, combining attributes akin to excellent team workflow tools like Slack and Intercom, all protected by a HIPAA-compliant security umbrella that healthcare industry organizations need.

 - I was a key engineer for the front-end platform at Glympse, writing cross-platform real-time location-sharing applications that work on all different types of devices from a single code base: computers, phones, TVs, and even refrigerators.

 - I was the architect for the implementation the entirety of Intel's global web properties (see intel.com) during their responsive re-branding/redesign (2014-2015).

 - I played the lead front-end development role in the v1.0 release of Microsoft's Band fitness tracker online dashboard, helping mesh creative, UX and development teams to build the product. (2014)

 - I was the team lead for Xbox.com before, during, and after the Xbox One launch, called "Microsoft's biggest launch in almost a decade" (2013-2014)

I am a trained designer, and excel at cross-discipline work. See my website for more:

www.laytonmiller.com

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Elegant Machine helps life sciences companies run patient journeys as one continuous AI-native operation across engagement, access, fulfillment, and ongoing support
positions.insights: Skills: AI Coding Tools · UX Engineering · Automated Software Testing · Product Design

positions.title: Senior Presentation Layer Engineer
positions.description:
I perform architectural and team lead roles writing code for large applications and web sites. Some of these include the 2015 global rebrand for Intel.com, the first release of the Microsoft Band web application, which was the desktop equivalent to the phone application, writing Win8 Metro applications and various campaign pages. I worked in a Presentation Layer Architect capacity.

I spent my first 8 months at Razorfish as the team lead for Xbox.com. We maintained and ran a very large number of the major titles on the Xbox.com website, as well as the main page and other large campaign pages such as Xbox One and Xbox 360. I had a very large hand in the overhaul of the maintenance process for the Xbox.com website fulfilling presentation layer architect-level duties such as overall framework design, architecture of solutions for managing content, high and low-level design of pages for both the Xbox.com home page and a variety of major titles such as Ryse, Forza 5, Dead Rising 3, Xbox Fitness, Xbox One campaign page, Xbox 360 campaign page, and many others.

positions.title: Owner
positions.description:
I ran (and still occasionally do) my own personal freelance design studio- Design Mill. I did everything from print design to web design to development and even video work. It was how I got started on my journey as a web professional and you can see the site with my somewhat out-of-date portfolio here:
www.desmill.com

positions.title: Presentation Layer Developer
positions.description: I am highly proficient in most front-end technologies including HTML, Javascript, CSS, jQuery, WinJS, AJAX, XML, JSON, Flash/Actionscript, and their typical back-ends such as Java, PHP and MySQL. I have gotten to utilize these skills on projects for clients like Microsoft, Razorfish, Express, Nokia, and more.

positions.title: CTO
positions.description: New Car City is a service similar to TrueCar that allows customers to search for new cars in their area. As CTO, I drove design and development efforts to construct the full stack for the V1 application before leaving after being offered a position as development lead at Xbox.

positions.title: Vice President, Director of Development & Design
positions.description: Designed, built, and maintained a number of proprietary systems to manage leads, support websites constructed for usage with the system, and manage inventories and other data for dealerships across the state of Washington.

positions.title: Chief of Online Operations
positions.description:
A previous client of mine, Jason Kettlestrings, realized that the amount of work I had done for his company merited my being around to oversee his new systems. Since I had personally engineered and coded his entire front-end, back-end, and content management systems (none of that Joomla stuff), he offered me 30% of the company and a more-than-fancy title to stick around and help him develop his company.
It was a fantastic experience.

honors.title: New Employee MVP
honors.description: I was awarded the new team member MVP award among Razorfish Seattle's 400+ employees for providing outstanding work and support to clients during an incredibly difficult tenure as Xbox.com team lead during the Xbox One launch.
honors.issuer: Issued by Razorfish Seattle Management · Jun 2014

volunteerExperiences.description: I founded and ran a Tango group that had hundreds of students over the years at Western Washington University. I built it to last, and it is currently thriving under it's third generation of instructors. I spent about a year and a half giving the same, non-profit classes for the Seattle chapter of the same group when I moved to Seattle.

projects.title: Microsoft Health Dashboard
projects.description:
We were engaged by Microsoft Health to provide consulting on the dashboard of their new Band product. CrUX and front-end development were provided to create the initial look, feel, and functionality of the dashboard tied into their backend API. We worked tightly with their internal teams and eventually handed off entirely to them as the dashboard went live.

Technology: Standard web technologies for front end tied to robust backend APIs. Complex cloud distribution scheme for geo-distributed load-balancing and caching.

projects.title: Microsoft Retail Holiday Gift Guide
projects.description: A small Microsoft project for holiday product showcasing on retailer sites.
